why: A pin asserted CONTAINMENT while every `why` in pinned-conjuncts.json is written as a DEMAND, and the two come apart under one operator. The recheck kept all three pinned conjuncts of criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 verbatim and disjoined each with `present(/payload/agreed_terms)`, a field records.schema.json requires of every SalesAgreement -- so every `any` is satisfied unconditionally and the criterion stopped requiring the agreement to name its Fulfillment, that Fulfillment to be `delivered`, or any Obligation to be `discharged` or `transferred`. Measured at exit 0, 269,592 checks, 31 of 31 fixtures still rejecting, with the pin file, the fixtures and the `requires` prose all untouched. This fixture performs exactly that hunk and requires the validator to reject it, naming the disjunction rather than reporting the conjunct as missing -- it is not missing, and a message that said so would send a reader to look for something that is right there.
expect_failure_contains: PINNED CONJUNCT ONLY UNDER A DISJUNCTION
note: The positive control matters more here than in r13: the mutation must REGENERATE cleanly, because a hunk that crashes author_phase_content.py proves only that the DSL rejected it. The runner reports FAIL rather than a rejection if regeneration fails. And if this fixture is ever rejected for a reason OTHER than the disjunction -- the runner checks the message -- then something weaker is refusing it and the demand rule has stopped carrying its own weight.
